no-restricted-properties.message: `JSON.parse` returns `any`, and that `any` flows unchecked into every read downstream, which is where most no-unsafe findings come from. Parse through @nexus/source/structured-text/json/Json instead: `parseJsonOrThrow(text, context, isValue)` with a guard from @nexus/source/validation/Guard when the code reads fields, or `parseJson(text, context)` and handle its 'Invalid' outcome where bad input already falls back. Name the source in `context`. For a deep clone, use `structuredClone`.

no-restricted-globals.name: Buffer
no-restricted-globals.message: `Buffer` is the Node global, and it does not exist on Cloudflare Workers, which is why @cloudflare/workers-types declares it `any`: nothing read through it is checked. Use the byte helpers in @nexus/source/encoding/ByteEncoding instead: utf8ToBytes / bytesToUtf8, base64ToBytes / bytesToBase64, base64UrlToBytes / bytesToBase64Url, hexToBytes / bytesToHex, concatenateBytes, utf8ByteLength, byteView, and `new Uint8Array(length)` for Buffer.alloc. A Buffer a Node API hands back (readFileSync, cipher.update) is already typed; keep using it as the Uint8Array it is..

reasons.no-unused-private-class-members: The core rule sees only #private names. @typescript-eslint/no-unused-private-class-members, on here, is the typed rule that supersedes it.
reasons.guard-for-in: nexus/consistency-no-for-in bans for...in outright, guarded or not, so there is no loop left for this rule to guard.
reasons.no-invalid-this: @typescript-eslint/no-invalid-this, on here, is the same rule taught TypeScript's this parameters.
reasons.require-atomic-updates: It flags any write after an await to something read before it, and on ahra none of its 39 findings was a read-modify-write. nexus/concurrency-no-lost-update replaces it, firing only when the written value is computed from the same location read before the suspension.
reasons.no-loop-func: Block-scoped let and const already give each iteration its own binding, and no-var forbids the var that shared one, so the bug it guards is a var-era one.
reasons.@typescript-eslint/no-dynamic-delete: Taste wearing a correctness badge: TypeScript already owns the real hazard.
reasons.@typescript-eslint/prefer-enum-initializ: nexus/consistency-no-enum bans enums, so this could only fire inside a construct already refused.
reasons.@typescript-eslint/prefer-literal-enum-m: nexus/consistency-no-enum bans enums, so this could only fire inside a construct already refused.
reasons.no-eq-null: eqeqeq already forbids every ==, == null included, so this rule only reported the same line a second time.
reasons.no-await-in-loop: It cannot tell a loop that must be sequential from one that need not be: on ahra about three in four of its findings were pagination, retries, polling or ordered output. nexus/performance-no-independent-await-in-loop replaces it, firing only where the iterations are provably independent.
reasons.@typescript-eslint/non-nullable-type-ass: Its fix writes x!, which @typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion forbids, so the two rules contradict each other.
reasons.@typescript-eslint/init-declarations: TypeScript's definite-assignment analysis already refuses a read before assignment. With no mode the rule checks nothing, and set to always it forces = undefined placeholders that blind that analysis.
reasons.no-implicit-globals: moduleDetection force makes every file a module, so there is no global scope left to leak into.
reasons.@typescript-eslint/no-restricted-types: With no ban list it checks nothing, and no type is banned yet.
reasons.consistent-return: Ruled by Kirk on 2026-08-25: it cannot see types, so it flags exhaustive switches the checker proves end and effects typed void | Destructor. noImplicitReturns catches the real fall-off-the-end bug, and nexus/consistency-require-matching-return-type rules the return forms.
reasons.prefer-promise-reject-errors: @typescript-eslint/prefer-promise-reject-errors, on here, is the type-aware version of the same rule.
reasons.no-implied-eval: @typescript-eslint/no-implied-eval, on here, reads types, so it catches an alias of setTimeout the core rule sees only by name.
reasons.no-inline-comments: We write trailing comments on purpose (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.prefer-destructuring: Destructuring turns a property into a naked local, the opposite of Reach Over Alias (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.@typescript-eslint/consistent-return: Kirk's ruling on core consistent-return holds for its typed twin: noImplicitReturns and nexus/consistency-require-matching-return-type carry it (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.default-case: @typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check is the type-aware version, and a default would hide a missed union member (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.sort-vars: One declaration per statement is the house form, and a declaration with one declarator has nothing to sort (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.no-continue: Style, with no bug class behind it (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.id-length: Style, and nexus/consistency-no-abbreviated-identifier already rules names (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.class-methods-use-this: Style: Base's dependency-injected services are classes by design, so a method that never reads this is ordinary (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.no-plusplus: Style, with no bug class behind it (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.no-negated-condition: Style, with no bug class behind it (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.complexity: A threshold, not a defect (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.func-name-matching: Style, with no bug class behind it (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.max-depth: A threshold, not a defect (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.no-underscore-dangle: Style, and many of the names it flags are external grammar like __typename (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.no-bitwise: Hashes, colors and audio use bitwise operators on purpose (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.id-denylist: It does nothing without a list, and the house's name bans live in nexus/ rules (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.id-match: It does nothing without a pattern, and casing is ruled by nexus/consistency-require-constant-casing (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.no-restricted-exports: It does nothing without a list, and no export name is banned (#e4cn6wq Block 4).
reasons.no-restricted-imports: It does nothing without a list: api writes one where it needs one, and ahra and www ban sources through nexus/import-no-forbidden-source (#e4cn6wq Block 4).

overrides.reason: A generator's output is as long as the schema it prints, so its length measures the schema rather than a seam anyone chose. Every other rule holds generated code to the house standard (#c076xbg); max-lines alone does not apply (#50tpzjq).
